points.title: Plagiarism
points.must: Presenting another person's work, words, ideas, images or code as your own without acknowledging the source.

points.title: Source, citation, academic integrity
points.must: Source = work information is taken from; citation tells who, when, where; academic integrity = honest work with every source acknowledged.

points.title: Forms of plagiarism
points.must: At least five forms with an example each: direct copy-paste, mosaic / patchwriting, paraphrase without citation, translation, self-plagiarism, code, ghost-writing / AI, incorrect citation.

points.title: Why it is a problem and consequences
points.must: Dishonest, unfair, no learning, may break copyright; consequences at school, exams, university, work.

points.title: Anti-plagiarism resource
points.must: A program / service that compares a document with a large database of texts and produces a similarity report.

points.title: Similarity score
points.must: Percentage of text matching the databases; originality = 100 % − similarity; it measures matching text, not plagiarism.

points.title: How a document is checked
points.must: Upload → fragments and fingerprints → compare with web pages, publications, submitted papers → matches highlighted with sources → similarity report.

points.title: Examples of resources
points.must: Turnitin, Antiplagiat, StrikePlagiarism and others; MOSS / JPlag for program code; exact-phrase search.

points.title: Free vs institutional checker
points.must: Free checkers mostly search web pages; institutional ones also have publications and an archive of submitted work.

points.title: Limitations
points.must: Sources not in the database, paraphrasing / translation, images and ideas, false positives, privacy; a human must interpret.

points.title: Checking your own document
points.must: Final draft → upload → open every highlighted passage → exclude quotes / bibliography → fix (quote + reference, cite, rewrite) → check again.

points.title: Reading a report (worked example)
points.must: Each match judged: quoted and cited = acceptable; copied without acknowledgement = plagiarism; reference list / common phrase = false positive.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: Similarity % treated as proof; 0 % as proof of originality; synonym-swapping to beat the checker.
